title: The God Who Provides and Sustains

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Worship the Lord your God, and his blessing will be on your food and water. I will take away sickness from among you, and none will miscarry or be barren in your land, and I will give you a full life span." - Exodus 23:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God connects wholehearted worship with His care over His people's lives — their food, their water, their health, their families. These were covenant promises given to Israel in their particular time and setting, and we must be careful not to twist them into a guarantee that faithful believers today will never face sickness or loss. That would be a false and cruel promise, and Scripture itself shows godly people who suffered. Yet within these words shines an unchanging truth about who God is.

Our God is a provider and a sustainer. He is deeply attentive to the daily needs of His people — the bread on the table, the water in the well, the health of the body. He is not a distant deity indifferent to whether we eat or thrive. The same heart that pledged to bless Israel's food and water still cares tenderly about your provision and your wellbeing today. Jesus taught us to ask for our daily bread, confident that our Father knows exactly what we need (Matt 6:11, 32).

So while we do not claim these as blanket promises of a trouble-free life, we can rest fully in the character behind them. Whatever we face — even sickness, even loss — we are held by a God who provides, sustains, and works all things for our ultimate good (Rom 8:28). And He promises us something greater than a long earthly life: eternal life with Him, where sickness and sorrow are gone forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I trust God as my faithful provider and sustainer, even in hard times?
How does the promise of eternal life anchor me when earthly life is difficult?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are my provider and sustainer, attentive to my every need. Help me trust Your care even in hardship, resting in Your goodness and the eternal life You promise. Amen.
